claims.text: Test by the suspected cause: imaging for abdominal or brain causes; specific blood tests or cultures for inherited metabolic disease or serious infection.
claims.quote: Testing should be directed by suspected causative disorders (see table Some Causes of Vomiting in Infants, Children, and Adolescents ). Imaging studies are typically done to evaluate abdominal or central nervous system pathology. Various specific blood tests or cultures are done to diagnose inherited metabolic disorders or serious infection.

claims.text: Serum electrolytes with suspected dehydration or prolonged vomiting.
claims.quote: If dehydration is suspected, or vomiting has been prolonged, serum electrolytes should be measured.

claims.text: Bilious vomiting means a high intestinal obstruction; in an infant it needs immediate evaluation.
claims.quote: Bilious vomiting indicates a high intestinal obstruction and, especially in an infant, requires immediate evaluation

claims.text: Abdominal pain with vomiting: ultrasound is the first-line imaging in children.
claims.quote: Ultrasonography is the imaging choice for acute abdominal pain in children.
